content: 1. Tecovirimat reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Monitor closely when co-administered, as tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Adjust therapy as needed to ensure the effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 2. Erythromycin stearate and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. This combination requires close monitoring or therapy modification to mitigate the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. 3. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of temocillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 4. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered to avoid potential toxicity. 5. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of the P-gp substrate as per product labeling. 6. Erythromycin stearate and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative therapy to prevent serious cardiac complications. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen when co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. Monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent toxicity. 9. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Thioridazine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative therapy to reduce the risk of torsades de pointes. 11. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent adverse effects. 13. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No specific dose adjustment is recommended with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, but reduce the tofacitinib dose if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent toxicity. 16. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid P-gp inhibitors; the interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of toremifene by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid co-administration with agents that prolong the QT interval. If unavoidable, interrupt toremifene therapy or closely monitor the patient with ECGs. 20. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tramadol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may require a reduced tramadol dose or adjustment of dosing intervals. Monitor closely for serious adverse events, including seizures and serotonin syndrome. 22. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as both agents prolong the QTc interval. 23. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Trifluoperazine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative therapy. 26. Erythromycin stearate and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Trimipramine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative therapy. 28. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 29. Trofinetide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid co-administration with sensitive substrates. 30. Erythromycin stearate and tropisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 33. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Erythromycin stearate and valbenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of valoctocogene roxaparvovec by potentiating hepatotoxicity. Monitor closely and consider alternative medications. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of valproic acid by inhibiting its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of valsartan by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Erythromycin stearate and vandetanib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor ECGs more frequently. 39. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the vardenafil dose to 5 mg per 24 hours and monitor closely. 40. Vemurafenib and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin may also increase vemurafenib levels. 41. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicity. 42. Erythromycin stearate and venlafaxine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of verapamil by the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 44. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur, reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of vincristine and vincristine liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of vitamin K1 (phytonadione) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Erythromycin stearate and voclosporin both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin stearate also increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 51. Erythromycin stearate and voriconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Voriconazole also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 52. Vorinostat and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 53. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while erythromycin stearate decreases the levels of zafirlukast by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is uncertain, but monitoring is advised. 54. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 56. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of zavegepant intranasal by inhibiting OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 57. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both agents prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Common adverse effects of erythromycin stearate include abdominal pain (8%), headache (8%), nausea (8%), diarrhea (7%), rash (3%), vomiting (3%), dyspepsia (2%), flatulence (2%), pain (2%), pruritus (1%), and pseudomembranous colitis.
